newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pannon bonds start trading on Budapest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Pannon bonds start trading on Budapest bourse.

text.p: Three inflation-indexed bonds of Hungarian mobile phone company Pannon GSM started trading on Wednesday on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
Pannon has issued a nominal 25 billion forints of three, four and five-year bonds with an interest rate of CPI plus three percent, the company said in a statement.
Most of the money raised will be spent on the company's expansion plans, such as doubling both subscriber number and sales in 1997.
The company had 170,000 subscribers -- or a 37 percent market share -- at the end of 1996 and had sales of some 18.5 billion forints last year.

Prices for the three-year Pannon GSM 2000/A bonds stand at 101 percent of the 10,000 forints nominal value, the four-year B series price stands at 101.1 percent and the five-year C series traded at 101.2 percent at 10:43 GMT.
